html:
Île Sainte-Marie, a small island off the east coast of Madagascar, was the main base of pirates in the Indian Ocean from the 1690s to the 1720s.

Pirates from the Caribbean and North America sailed there to raid ships carrying Indian goods and Muslim pilgrims in the Red Sea and the Arabian Sea. A New York trader set up a post there in 1691 to sell them supplies, and Captain William Kidd called there in 1698.

Some pirates married into local families, and their descendants, the Zana-Malata, founded the Betsimisaraka confederation on the east coast in the 18th century. The pirates' attacks on the Mughal ships helped push European trading companies and navies to police the Indian Ocean, ending the golden age of piracy.
sum: Île Sainte-Marie, a small island off the east coast of Madagascar, was the main base of pirates in the Indian Ocean from the 1690s to the 1720s.
